evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 花 entry; standard form, pronunciation, dated senses
evidence.text: The entry says 花 is not recorded in Shuowen. It gives modern Mandarin huā and quotes Tang examples for the noun ‘flower’ (段成式, 崔護) and verb ‘to flower’ (杜甫). Its further senses include flower-like objects, beauty, patterns, variety, expenditure, and others, but the displayed citations do not establish a dated chain linking those extensions.
evidence.title: A03439 花 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Wikisource, received text of Shuowen Jiezi
evidence.text: The received Shuowen text defines 𠌶 as the flower of grasses and trees, analyzing it as 从𠂹亏聲; 華 is defined as flourishing and analyzed as 从艸从𠌶. This is the Han-period lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of original graphic design.
evidence.title: 說文解字/06

evidence.source: Li Guisen and Liu Hongtao, Tsinghua University Research Center for Excavated Texts
evidence.text: The authors argue that early forms depict a plant and open flower, with graphic simplification and later alteration making the flower strokes resemble 𠂹. They propose that Shuowen consequently misanalyzed the form. This is their scholarly interpretation; it conflicts with Shuowen’s account and should not be stated as settled fact.
evidence.title: 釋“華”及相關諸字

evidence.source: Li Guisen and Liu Hongtao, Tsinghua University Research Center for Excavated Texts
evidence.field: Warring States uses and graphic relations among 華 forms
evidence.text: The authors report Warring States manuscript 芋 used for 華, including flower/flourishing contexts. They propose that 華 developed from a flower graph with an added 艸 classifier, and discuss 春秋-period 華 examples. Their account distinguishes these graphs from later 花; it does not demonstrate a continuous sequence into 花.
evidence.title: 釋“華”及相關諸字

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: research note on 花 and related forms
evidence.text: The dictionary reports that Shuowen has entries for 𠌶 and 華 but not 花, and describes later 花 as using 化 for sound. It also reports Wang Niansun’s analysis of an older variant with 艸 and 白 whose sound was like 化. These are dictionary summaries of historical scholarship, not a dated first attestation of 花.
evidence.title: A03439 花 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 韻典網, Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese phonology database
evidence.field: 花 phonetic-series assignment and comparative readings
evidence.text: The entry assigns 花 to phonetic 化 and gives Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese hʷraː, with Middle Chinese comparisons including xwa (Karlgren and Wang Li), xua (Li Rong and Shao Rongfen), hɣua (Zhengzhang), hʷɯa (Pan Wuyun), and hwaɨ (Pulleyblank). These are reconstructions or transcriptions in their named systems, not ancient recordings.
evidence.title: 花 - 字 - 上古音系 - 韻典網

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 花 entry, reporting Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang systems
evidence.text: The page gives Mandarin huā and reconstructions Baxter–Sagart *qʷʰˤra and Zhengzhang *hʷraː; it identifies 化 as the sound component in its Zhengzhang table. Together with the separate 化 comparison in the dossier, this supports a plausible later sound-component analysis. Because the systems differ and the available independent 化 comparison is not a primary attestation, this does not establish the graph’s date or exact original pronunciation.
evidence.title: 花 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.text: The file page identifies the image as an SVG representation of a Shuowen seal-script style character, attributes its source to S04460 on the 華 entry, and marks the representation public domain. This is a modern digital redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

search_audit.outcome: Opened the Shuowen text and Zhengzhang database page and inspected their contents. Search results exposed Baxter–Sagart comparison data, but direct opening and in-page lookup of that PDF returned internal errors; no direct inspection claim is made for that source.

gaps: No primary dated first occurrence of the graph 花 was established. The MOE entry supplies Tang citations for flower and flowering senses, while secondary accounts differ on when 花 emerged.

The received Shuowen analysis of 𠌶 differs from the Tsinghua study’s proposed flower depiction and account of graphic alteration. The Tsinghua paper provides a scholarly alternative, not a settled correction.

The relation of later 花 to older 𠌶/華 is reported as spelling or variant history, but the inspected sources do not establish an uninterrupted dated graphic sequence. Component roles in the later 花 graph must not be transferred to those older forms.

化’s role as sound component is supported by modern dictionaries and a Zhengzhang-series database, but no independently inspected primary reconstruction table for 化 was obtained in this search. Historical reconstructions are theoretical comparisons, not direct ancient pronunciations.
Tang attestations support flower and ‘to flower’; dates and semantic links for later senses such as spending, pattern, beauty, and indistinctness remain unestablished here.
